rv.q: "Sarah Ruhl has written an amiable hour about monogamy and its discontents...Then, unfortunately, Ruhl inserts an intermission, spins out 35 more minutes of chatty whimsy...A light, frolicsome one-act mutates into a mediocre marriage play...If 'How to Transcend' were a tryst, it would be two hours of light foreplay followed by your partner...
But ultimately, the lasting impression is less than the sum of its parts.
All this is on display in "How To Transcend a Happy Marriage," but this play doesn’t come together as effectively as some of her previous theater that touches on similar territory.

cn.t: Sarah Ruhl's comedy about polyamory features strong performances and sharp dialogue, but critics find the mix of realism and surreal elements bewildering, with the whole never quite coming together despite amusing moments.
